Distributed Secrets Manager

Three real server processes replicate encrypted state, lose a leader, elect a replacement, and bring the restarted node back up to date.

01:15raft failure lab · local three-node cluster

01.1

Raft replication

The leader authenticates the request, encrypts the new version, and appends only ciphertext to its write-ahead log. Success waits for a majority—not merely a local disk write.

node 03followerreplicating
2 / 3 → committed
01.2

Envelope encryption

Each secret version receives a fresh data key. A vault-wide encryption key wraps those data keys; a root key protects the vault key. Rotation can replace wrapping keys without touching every encrypted payload.

[ root key ]split into recovery shares
│ wraps
[ vault KEK ]unlocked only in memory
│ wraps
[ version DEK ]new random key per version
│ encrypts + AAD
{ ciphertext }bound to path + version

failure model

Handles leader loss, process restarts, and lagging followers through log recovery, leader election, divergence repair, and quorum enforcement.

02 / operating systems · virtualization

VM Resource
Coordinator

Two C control loops manage vCPU placement and memory allocation for KVM/QEMU guests through libvirt. The CPU controller updates vCPU-to-host-CPU pinning from measured load; the memory controller responds to guest pressure and reclaims idle memory through ballooning.

  • C
  • Linux
  • libvirt
  • KVM
  • QEMU

VM Resource Coordinator

A web-based laboratory automates VM lifecycle, workload scenarios, and live performance analysis for both controllers.

01:25libvirt · live KVM guests

02.1

vCPU scheduling

The scheduler samples vCPU time, estimates utilization, and pins virtual CPUs to host CPU cores. It seeks a balanced host while avoiding needless migrations once the load is stable.

02.2

Memory coordination

The coordinator expands pressured guests and gradually reclaims unused capacity through ballooning. Guest floors and a host reserve remain hard constraints, even when every VM wants more.
